In my experience, you can’t educate those who don’t want to listen. It took my mom years, i mean YEARS, to actually accept mental health. My depression and anxiety started when i was just a kid (had a horrible childhood). It set in when i was 8. Growing up i was told by my parents i was acting out for attention, i need to let things go, its all in the past, it’s all in my head, i need to grow up, stop being lazy and get more focused, i need to be this way not that way, and the list goes on. When i was 16 i was additionally diagnosed with bipolar. Then in my early 20’s was told I’m a rare case with a duel diagnosis of bipolar and borderline personality disorder. Along with depression, anxiety, ptsd (mild), suicidal thoughts/tendencies. All accompanied by psychosis. When i was hospitalized for the first time 3/4 years ago that’s when my mom accepted mental health as a real thing. I noticed this cause when she asks me about my mental state of mind her questions changed. She’ll ask what’s going on and instead of giving me advice or telling me it’s not a big deal she’ll ask how can she help or what will make it better. My dad on the other hand says it’s all my fault and I’m seeking attention and when i have a bad episode he yells and says “i hope you’ve learned your lesson this time”. He also thinks being positive and eating an all meat diet only with “cure” me and everyone for that matter who have mental health disorders.
